reason: The cited evidence shows Cr addition reduces oxidation in a different alloy system (E1) and that CrTaO₄ can be protective in a non-equiatomic alloy (E2, E3), but no evidence supports the specific in-situ reaction of a thin Cr film on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, the predicted 50–70% reduction, or the claim that mechanical properties will be unaffected; E4 merely states coatings are needed without testing one.
premises: Cr addition improves oxidation resistance in refractory high-entropy alloys
CrTaO₄ can form a protective oxide layer on Cr- and Ta-containing RHEAs
A thin Cr film can react with substrate Ta to form CrTaO₄ in situ
A ~100 nm Cr coating will not degrade the alloy's mechanical properties
CrTaO₄ formation will reduce oxygen ingress by ~50–70% at 1000 °C for 100 h
